Agent.text: Every check passes: the build, the screenshot and all self-test steps. Wrapping up the notes.

I built the Painting Colour Assistant. It builds, starts and draws correctly, and its automatic test passes all 10 steps. You start in **Palettes**, where you make palettes like "Watercolor 1" and "Acrylic 1". You add paints from a library of 45 common pigments, or type in your own name, pigment code, colour and transparency (transparent, half-transparent or opaque). Each palette shows a chart of what every pair of its paints makes when mixed.

In **Painting** you choose watercolor, acrylic or oil and one of your palettes. Then you open a picture and crop it. You can view it in greyscale, as 2–10 value levels or as 2–24 colour levels, and lay a rule-of-thirds, Fibonacci spiral or grid over it. Every colour level gets a Kubelka-Munk mixing recipe, such as "4 Cobalt Blue + 2 Crimson + 1 Yellow Deep, water: like coffee", with a rating of how close the mix comes. Clicking any spot on the picture gives a recipe for that spot. For watercolor, lighter colours come from adding water over white paper; for acrylic and oil they come from adding white paint.

There was no existing program to copy, so most numbers are my own choices, and the check can't confirm the app uses them exactly. The paint colours in the library are my estimates, not measurements, so recipes are a good guide but not exact. If you set each paint's colour to match your own tubes, the recipes will match better. In your example "Crimson PG__", PG is a code for green pigments, so I guessed PR206 for the crimson; you can change it in the Palettes screen. The "Open picture..." window wasn't tried by hand; dropping a picture file onto the window also works.

A good next request would be glazing: predicting how one transparent watercolor layer looks painted over another.

Agent.text: All checks pass. Updating the open question about mixing accuracy: the "only RGB" part is now settled, but the paint colours are still estimates.

Spektralni Kubelka-Munk prije nije bio ugrađen: boje su se miješale samo po crvenom, zelenom i plavom kanalu. Sada je ugrađen i zadano se koristi za recepte, tablicu miješanja u paletama i PDF. Aplikacija od boje svake tube izračuna glatku krivulju refleksije kroz 31 valnu duljinu (od 400 do 700 nm) i miješa boje valnu duljinu po valnu duljinu.

**Što se promijenilo za slikara:**
- Recepti su bliži stvarnoj boji. Grimizna i ftalo zelena sada daju neutralnu sivu, crvena i plava naginju prema ljubičastoj, a razrijeđena ftalo zelena ostaje zelena umjesto da postane neprirodno tirkizna. Stari način je u tim slučajevima griješio.
- Na probnoj slici recepti su u prosjeku točniji: razlika boja je 2,1 umjesto 3,0. Zato se postojeći recepti mogu promijeniti.
- Plavo i žuto ne daju zasićeniju zelenu nego prije, nego malo prigušeniju. Tekst pomoći je zato napisan prema tome što se stvarno dogodilo, a ne prema mom očekivanju.
- Ispod „Paints per mix” je novi prekidač „Mixing model” (Spectral / RGB) s objašnjenjem kad se pokazivač zadrži iznad njega. Tako se možete vratiti na stari način i usporediti. Svaka slika pamti svoj izbor, a PDF navodi koji je način korišten.

**Provjera:** aplikacija se gradi bez upozorenja za računalo i za web. Svih 25 automatskih provjera prolazi, uključujući četiri nove za ovu značajku. Pregledao sam snimke zaslona za široki prikaz, za mobitel i za zaslon s paletama.

**Što je ostalo otvoreno:**
- Krivulje boja su procjena izvedena iz jedne boje tube, nisu izmjerene. Prave boje mogu imati oštrije krivulje, pa recepte vrijedi usporediti s naslikanim uzorcima.
- I dalje je otvoreno pitanje o kodu „Crimson PG__” iz vašeg zahtjeva; zasad koristim PR206.
- Alat Craft Anything ne mjeri u radu programa vrijednosti iz popisa parametara, nego ih samo čita, pa one ostaju neprovjerene.

**Izvan mape `app/`:** prema uputama projekta ažurirao sam README, CHANGELOG i CLAUDE.md. Za web inačicu sam na ovo računalo instalirao Rustovu podršku za WebAssembly. Ništa nije commitano.

Sljedeće bi se moglo dodati unos izmjerenih krivulja boja ili tablicu stvarnih spektara za boje iz knjižnice pigmenata. Time bi recepti bili još bliži onome što nastaje na papiru.

There's now a **Mix / Glaze** switch beside the paints. In Glaze mode each colour becomes a layered recipe, such as "Cobalt Blue, then Crimson, then Lemon Yellow", with the strength of each layer and small swatches showing the colour after each one. Watercolour recipes start with a wash on the paper; acrylic and oil recipes start with one paint mixed with white, or the bare white ground. Up to two glazes of transparent or half-transparent paints go on top, each picture remembers the choice, and the PDF brochure lists the glazing recipes.

It builds, and all 30 steps of the automatic run-through pass, including new glazing checks for watercolour, acrylic and the PDF; I looked at the watercolour, oil and phone layouts on screen. With the starter palettes, glazing usually matches within the "excellent" to "good" range. Greens in the oil palette come out only "close" or "rough", because that palette has no transparent yellow or green. How thick each glaze strength is ("a veil", "thin", "strong" and so on) is my estimate, not measured from real paint, and the first layer is always a single paint rather than a mix.

I also updated the README, the changelog and the project notes outside the app folder, and added two screenshot options for showing Glaze mode and a chosen paint type. Nothing is committed yet. A good next step would be to paint one transparent colour at a few strengths over white and compare it with the swatches in the app, so the glaze strengths can be set from real paint.
